points.title: Entity
points.must: A thing (person, object, place or event) about which data is stored, e.g. Student, Book; each entity becomes a table.

points.title: Attribute
points.must: A property of an entity — one item of data stored about it, e.g. StudentID, Name; each attribute becomes a field.

points.title: Relationship
points.must: A link between two entities showing how their records are connected; in a database it is made with a primary key and a matching foreign key.

points.title: Entity-relationship diagram
points.must: A diagram showing entities (boxes), relationships (lines) and the degree of each relationship (1:1, 1:M, M:M); drawn at the design stage.

points.title: Finding entities in a description
points.must: Nouns with many records are entities, the details stored about them are attributes, the verbs linking two entities are relationships, a unique attribute is the identifier (primary key).

points.title: Entity, attribute or value
points.must: Entity → table, attribute → field, value → cell (e.g. Pupil / Class / 11A); something is a separate entity only if several facts are stored about it.

points.title: One-to-one
points.must: Each record in A is linked to at most one record in B and vice versa, with an example (person — passport, country — capital).

points.title: One-to-many
points.must: One record in A is linked to many in B, each record in B to only one in A, with an example (class — pupils) and which side is many.

points.title: Many-to-many
points.must: One record in A is linked to many in B and one in B to many in A, with an example (students — courses).

points.title: Asking in both directions
points.must: Ask "can one A have many B?" and "can one B have many A?": yes/no → 1:M, yes/yes → M:M, no/no → 1:1.

points.title: ERD notation
points.must: Rectangle = entity, line = relationship (labelled with a verb), 1 or a bar = one, crow's foot or M = many (at the many end), identifier underlined or marked PK.

points.title: Implementing 1:M and 1:1 with keys
points.must: 1:M: the primary key of the "one" table is placed as a foreign key in the "many" table; 1:1: a unique foreign key in one table (or merge the two tables).

points.title: Resolving M:M with a link table
points.must: M:M cannot be stored directly; it is replaced by a link (junction) table holding both primary keys as foreign keys (often a composite key), giving two 1:M relationships, with an example (Students — Enrolments — Courses).

points.title: Reading the foreign key
points.must: The table that contains the foreign key is on the "many" side of a 1:M relationship.

points.title: From an ERD to tables
points.must: Each entity → table, identifier → primary key; copy the PK of the "one" side into the "many" side; a link table for each M:M.

points.title: Steps to draw an ERD from a description
points.must: Find entities, list attributes and a primary key, find relationships (verbs), decide each degree by asking in both directions, resolve M:M, draw boxes and lines marking 1 or M and add foreign keys.
